entries.command:
docker compose -f labs/sql/_stack/compose.yaml exec -T \
  -e PGPASSWORD=demo-password postgres \
  psql -U support -d support_lab -A --pset=footer=off \
  -c "SELECT count(*) AS true_enterprise FROM customers WHERE plan = 'enterprise';"
aliases: select count(*) from customers where plan = 'enterprise';

entries.command:
docker compose -f labs/sql/_stack/compose.yaml exec -T \
  -e PGPASSWORD=demo-password postgres \
  psql -U support -d support_lab -A -F'|' --pset=footer=off \
  -c "SELECT c.id, c.name, u.email FROM customers c JOIN workspaces w ON w.customer_id = c.id JOIN users u ON u.workspace_id = w.id ORDER BY c.id LIMIT 12;"

docker compose -f labs/sql/_stack/compose.yaml exec -T \
  -e PGPASSWORD=demo-password postgres \
  psql -U support -d support_lab -A -F'|' --pset=footer=off \
  -c "SELECT c.plan, count(DISTINCT c.id) AS customers, count(*) AS result_rows FROM customers c JOIN workspaces w ON w.customer_id = c.id JOIN users u ON u.workspace_id = w.id GROUP BY c.plan ORDER BY c.plan;"

-- Active accounts report: customers with at least one user, by plan.
-- Edit this until it answers the question correctly, then run `tse check`.
SELECT c.plan, COUNT(*) AS customer_count
FROM customers c
JOIN workspaces w ON w.customer_id = c.id
JOIN users u ON u.workspace_id = w.id
GROUP BY c.plan
ORDER BY c.plan;
